parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
a duct is a pipe or channel

explanation.surface: A specialist commenting on what comes out of a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A product is something made or produced, which is what a factory's output consists of.

indicators.note: in places one item inside another

parts.note: a dump is slang for a bowel movement, poo
tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: A spoiled vegetable thrown away in the tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dump' looks like a rubbish tip but is the vulgar slang meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato is a starchy tuber eaten as a staple, an everyday kind of vegetable.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to prohibit by law
second meaning: either of the famous 1930s American bank robbers, fugitives from justice

explanation.definitionFit: To outlaw something is to make it illegal, and Bonnie Parker and Clyde Barrow were notorious criminals on the run.

clue.text: Wicked indecent exposure foolish senior ignored — surprising!

indicators.note: wicked behaviour is twisted, so the letters that follow are rearranged
foolish means silly or muddled, so that word's letters may come in any order
ignored letters are left out and play no part in the result

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written; these letters are removed in any order

explanation.surface: An old man caught flashing would be a shocking sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle all sixteen letters, then take out the six of the second word to leave the ten-letter answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unexpected comes as a surprise, so the adjective surprising means the same thing.

clue.text: Tool loses right to throw this in

definitions.note: refers to the idiom rather than giving a plain synonym

indicators.note: loses means something is taken away from the word

parts.note: a trowel is a small garden or building tool
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A tool loses its right to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: To throw in the towel is to give up, from a boxing trainer throwing a towel into the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of conceding defeat is throwing in the towel, so this is the cloth you throw in.

clue.text: Undresses, having taken drug in bars

indicators.note: having taken something in means holding it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to strip is to undress
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone takes off their clothes after taking a drug in some bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' looks like pubs, but it is the definition, in the sense of bands or lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripes are long narrow bands of colour, and bars is another word for such lines.

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters within another piece

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street

indicators.note: trouble stirs things up, so the preceding word's letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A clever researcher stirs up a riot on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: A boffin is British slang for a scientist or technical expert.
explanation.definitionFit: A boffin is informal British slang for a research scientist or technical expert.

indicators.note: partly means only a portion of the entry is used

parts.note: the middle letters of the answer to 5 across

explanation.surface: A remark that the striped item is half done.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 5 across is STRIPES, whose middle four letters give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that is ripe is ready to be eaten, so ripe means fully ready.

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
a piece of writing is an article

explanation.surface: A fragment of a piano composition.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle is a tiny fragment or speck of something, the same as a small bit.

indicators.note: catching means holding something, so one word goes around another

parts.note: to sway someone is to influence them
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: Someone exerting influence in a roundabout way while catching fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideways means at an angle rather than straight on, an oblique or indirect approach.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a handle is slang for a name or form of address
second meaning: a publisher counts each book it sells as one item of its list

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like verbs (manage, reserve), but each is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is a person's formal name, slangily a handle, and publishers call each individual book a title.

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the following word's letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone murmurs the grim news that his wife has died.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make the words look like what was said, but they are the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To whisper is to speak very softly, so whispered is the past tense meaning spoke in a low voice.

clue.text: Bouncy oriental MP bounces on this

definitions.note: a description of the thing rather than a noun

indicators.note: something bouncy jumps about, so the letters that follow are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lively politician from the East jumps up and down on something.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampoline is a sprung canvas frame people jump up and down on for fun or gymnastics.

parts.note: to vie is to compete
W is the abbreviation for western

explanation.surface: Rivalry with the Western point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a personal belief or way of seeing a matter, the same as an opinion.

indicators.note: out means disordered or wrong, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Inadequate officers taking time off work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incomplete is lacking a part, so it is deficient or not whole.

clue.text: Do join in now and again

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration, a special occasion
to ally is to join or unite with

explanation.surface: An invitation to come along every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb but is the noun for a social event.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasionally means from time to time, at irregular intervals, which is what now and again expresses.

clue.text: No amity is produced by this

definitions.text: No amity is produced by this

indicators.note: produced means made into something, so the letters are formed into a new word

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that this feeling creates no friendship at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Animosity is strong hostility, which is the opposite of amity, or friendliness, so it produces none.

clue.text: Dancing like me gives Disney energy

parts.note: Walt Disney, the animation pioneer
zing is vigour or energy

explanation.surface: The setter dances, inspired by Disney's liveliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Me' is the setter, Matilda, and Waltzing Matilda is the Australian folk song.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter Matilda points to the song title Waltzing Matilda, and waltzing is a form of dancing.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a British Sunday newspaper
second meaning: someone who sees an event happen

explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Observer is a well-known British Sunday title, and anyone who watches an event is an onlooker.

indicators.note: flying letters are scattered through the air and land in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Restrictions on flights over Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbreviation is a shortening of a word, and curtailment means cutting something short.

clue.text: I'm backing out of feminist play, it's most lightweight

indicators.note: to play with letters is to move them about into a new order
backing means moving backwards, so the word is read in the other direction
out of means taken from, so those letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written, then read backwards
taken as written, from which letters are removed

explanation.surface: A critic pulls out of a feminist play, dismissing it as the slightest of works.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M then I from the second word, leaving six letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Finest can mean thinnest or most delicate, as in finest thread, which is most lightweight.

clue.text: Was unfaithful, losing head when passionate

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: to cheat on a partner is to be unfaithful

explanation.surface: Someone strayed from a partner in the heat of the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated argument is an angry or impassioned one, so heated means full of strong feeling.

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Something coming up later in the news bulletin.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to the next one in surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Then means after that, at a subsequent time, which is the sense of later.

parts.note: a booby is a tropical seabird
spoils, as a noun, are goods won, a prize

explanation.surface: Continuing from the news, a bird ruins a wooden spoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoils' looks like a verb but is the noun meaning plunder. The wooden spoon is the joke award for coming last.
explanation.definitionFit: A booby prize is given to whoever finishes last in a contest, which is what the wooden spoon traditionally marks.

indicators.note: naughty letters misbehave and refuse to stay in their order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Behaving badly by overindulging in alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: To binge is to overindulge in a short spell, especially in alcohol, which is drinking to excess.

indicators.note: some means only part of the word that follows is used

parts.note: letters inside the word

explanation.surface: Beauty products intended for someone from South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca were the native people of the Andes who ruled a Peruvian empire, so an Inca is South American.

indicators.note: something renewable can be made over again, so these letters are made into a new form

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to welcome development that cannot be sustained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-renewable' reads as one word, but the hyphen splits it: 'non' is fodder and 'renewable' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An invention is a newly created device or process, a new development in technology.

clue.text: Affair the night before not without heart

indicators.note: without heart means the centre of the word is taken away

parts.note: the eve is the evening before a special day
taken as written before its centre goes

explanation.surface: An affair that happened the night before, but not without passion.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair can mean an occasion or happening, and an event is exactly such an occurrence.

parts.note: a bug is an infection, a germ
any means whichever one, it doesn't matter

explanation.surface: Any old infection will do.
explanation.definitionFit: Germany is a nation of central Europe, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: In bed etc, eleven turned in

indicators.note: turned means facing the other way, so the run of letters is read backwards
the last in says the letters lie inside the words before it

parts.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: A tired list of lying in bed and so on, eleven people going to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'In' is the definition, as a politician is in when voted into office; the last 'in' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A party that is in has won power, so it has been elected to office by the voters.
